rich_summary: Manthara’s manipulation drives Queen Kaikeyi into a calculated fury. Convinced that Rama’s coronation will doom her son Bharata, Kaikeyi swears drastic vows: she will neither eat, drink, adorn herself, nor live if Rama is crowned. Casting aside her ornaments, she collapses on the floor like a fallen celestial being and prepares a scheme. Meanwhile King Dasaratha, joyful after arranging Rama’s installation, goes to share the news with his beloved queen. Passing through the luxurious inner palace, he discovers instead that Kaikeyi has entered the “chamber of wrath.” Shocked, he finds her lying on the ground in disheveled misery. Deeply distressed and blinded by love, the aged king begs to know who offended her and rashly promises to grant any wish—even unjust punishments or rewards—unknowingly giving Kaikeyi the leverage that will soon change the fate of the kingdom.

highlight_spans.why: Kaikeyi’s extreme vow shows how deeply Manthara’s words have poisoned her mind and foreshadows the coming catastrophe.
The imagery of Kaikeyi lying like a fallen celestial emphasizes the epic’s recurring theme of moral fall from divine grace.
Dasaratha enters joyfully to share Rama’s coronation news, creating dramatic irony because the reader knows disaster is already unfolding.
The king discovering Kaikeyi on the ground is the emotional pivot—his love and alarm make him vulnerable to her coming demands.
Dasaratha’s reckless promise to grant anything she desires becomes the decisive turning point that enables Rama’s exile.

top_scenes.scene_text: Queen Kaikeyi lies on the palace floor in the chamber of wrath, jewels scattered like fallen stars around her as her hair hangs disheveled and her face burns with anger.
King Dasaratha enters the opulent inner palace gardens filled with parrots, peacocks, and golden altars, unaware that the joyful news of Rama’s coronation is about to turn into tragedy.
The aged king kneels beside Kaikeyi lying in the dust, gently lifting her while promising to grant any wish, his face full of anxious devotion.
